title: A fit or seizure — protect their head and wait it out
applies_to: Someone whose body is shaking or has gone stiff, and who cannot answer you while it is happening.

citations.source: WHO and IFRC International First Aid, Resuscitation and Education Guidelines 2020
European Resuscitation Council Guidelines 2021: First Aid

steps.text: Look at a clock and note the time it started. How long it lasts matters more than anything else you can tell the doctor.
Move hard, hot, and sharp things away from them. Leave the person where they are unless they are in danger.
Put something soft under their head, such as a folded coat.
Let the shaking run its course. Watch it, stay close, and keep other people back.
Call for an ambulance if it lasts longer than 5 minutes, if another one starts, or if this is their first ever fit.
When the shaking stops, roll them onto their side with the mouth pointing slightly down.
Check that the chest is rising and falling normally. Stay with them while they come round.
Speak quietly and tell them where they are and what happened. They may be confused and frightened for a while.
Tell the ambulance crew how long it lasted and what you saw.

do_not: Do not hold them down or try to stop the shaking.
Do not put anything in their mouth, not even your fingers. Nobody can swallow their own tongue.
Do not give them anything to eat or drink until they are fully awake.
Do not leave them lying on their back once the shaking has stopped.
Do not crowd round them. Give them room and some privacy while they come round.
escalate_if: It lasts longer than 5 minutes, or another one starts before they wake up — call now.
They do not start breathing normally once the shaking stops — start pushing on the chest.
They are pregnant, hurt themselves, or it happened in water — call an ambulance whatever else happens.
It is a young child who is hot to touch — say that on the phone.
They do not come back to their normal self within about an hour — get them seen.
